name: @projexlight/connector-zendesk
summary: Zendesk connector: OAuth install + ticket / macro / automation sync. Lets a ProjexCloud support workflow surface as Zendesk tickets (and vice versa) so customer-facing teams keep using the Zendesk UI while back-office automation runs through ProjexCloud SDKs.

events.name: connector-zendesk.ticket.created.v1
events.description: Ticket created in Zendesk from a ProjexCloud event.

events.name: connector-zendesk.ticket.updated.v1
events.description: Inbound ticket update from Zendesk webhook.

events.name: connector-zendesk.macro.invoked.v1
events.description: Zendesk macro fired on a synced ticket; surfaced to sdk-workflow.

hooks.name: createTicket
hooks.description: Create a Zendesk ticket against a ProjexCloud entity.

hooks.name: syncMacros
hooks.description: Pull current macros + automations into the local cache.

scenarios.title: Tenant connects their Zendesk subdomain
scenarios.when_to_use: Admin grants OAuth; we store refresh token + record the subdomain.
scenarios.example_code:
import { installConnector } from '@projexlight/connector-zendesk';
const { install_id } = await installConnector({ tenant_id, subdomain: 'acme', auth_code });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Install row; vault-wrapped refresh token. Emits .install.created.v1.

scenarios.title: Failed sync creates a Zendesk ticket for the customer-success team
scenarios.when_to_use: When a connector sync fails repeatedly, we open a Zendesk ticket so CS has a tracked work item — not just a Slack notification.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Ticket created; ID stored on the originating ProjexCloud entity. Emits .ticket.created.v1.

scenarios.title: Webhook propagates ticket status to ProjexCloud entity
scenarios.when_to_use: Inbound ticket update — status change, comment added; we mirror to the linked ProjexCloud row.
scenarios.example_code:
import { handleWebhook } from '@projexlight/connector-zendesk';
await handleWebhook({ tenant_id, signature, body });

scenarios.title: Daily macro sync mirrors automation rules
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer's Zendesk macros change; we sync nightly so a ProjexCloud workflow editor can reference them.
scenarios.example_code:
import { syncMacros } from '@projexlight/connector-zendesk';
await syncMacros({ install_id });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Cache hydrated. .sync.completed.v1 emitted with row counts.

scenarios.title: Macro fires → sdk-workflow advances the linked workflow
scenarios.when_to_use: A Zendesk macro fires (e.g. 'mark resolved + email customer'); we surface it as an event so a ProjexCloud workflow can advance.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Workflow advances on the macro signal; audit chain pins the macro ID.

compliance_posture.notes: Refresh tokens vault-wrapped. Webhook signature verification mandatory. HIPAA tenants pin to Zendesk Enterprise + restrict ticket-body PII via the masking config.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per ticket created or updated outbound
